title: [Residence for Marshall and Nannie S. Field, 1905 South Prairie Avenue, Chicago, Illinois]. [First floor plan].
creator: Hunt, Richard Morris, 1827-1895 (architect); office of R. M. Hunt
repository: Library of Congress Prints & Photographs Division
collection: The Hunt Collection in the AIA/AAF Collection (Library of Congress); gift of American Institute of Architects / American Architectural Foundation, 2010 (DLC/PP-2010:100)
rights_basis: LoC: No known restrictions on publication.
found_via: loc.gov/pictures search 'Marshall Field 1905 Prairie' (fo=json); dimensions read from the 9256×13948 master TIFF
notes: Original office copy of Hunt's plan of the principal floor, inked and watercolour-washed: sheet headed 'Office Copy', 'No 2', 'M. FIELD', 'House for Marshall Field — Chicago Ill.', 'Plan of Principal Floor', 'Scale 1/4" = 1 ft', stamped 'This Drawing to be returned to R.M. Hunt Archt.' Rooms named: Drawing Room, Parlor(?), Library, Hall, Dining Room (octagonal), Conservatory (segmental bay), Main Stairs (circular, ~30 risers numbered), Service Stairs, Butler's Pantry, Closet; front entrance stoop and side steps drawn. Pencil annotations on finishes ('oak wainscot', 'black walnut wainscot'). The only located architect's drawing of any Prairie Avenue house found in this pass other than the Glessner set. Design-stage (1871–73) not as-built; Field house was altered (notably for later family use and 1905–06) — check against the 1886 Robinson atlas footprint and 1911 Sanborn before using. LoC dates and titles from Sam Watters (2024); published as fig. 3.16b in Watters, The Gilded Life of Richard Morris Hunt (2024).
